 Phoenix families who have lost SNAP, CHIP benefits can apply for help with bills
 KJZZ | 
 By
 Katherine Davis-Young 
 Published November 5, 2026 at 2:30 PM MST
 Facebook 
 Threads 
 LinkedIn 
 Bluesky 
 Email 
 Listen • 0:40
 Getty Images 
 / 
 Stock Glasses, pen and calculator on bills. 
 After hundreds of thousands of Arizonans lost SNAP benefits , the city of Phoenix created a crisis assistance program to help those households with bills . Now, the city is expanding eligibility for the program to include families with children who have recently lost health coverage.
 More than 22,000 Arizonans — mostly legally present refugees — lost eligibility for the state’s Medicaid program , AHCCCS, on Oct. 1 as new federal Medicaid rules took effect.
 Arizona was one of just a few states where children were included in cuts to coverage.
 Phoenix families whose kids lost coverage through the Children's Health Insurance Program, or CHIP, after Oct. 1 will now also be able to apply for the city’s one-time crisis assistance program.
 The program does not replace food benefits or healthcare. But it aims to help families make ends meet with a $600 credit toward utility bills and $100 for either gas or public transportation.
 The Phoenix City Council budgeted $3.15 million for the program, which launched in July.
 More than 1,000 Phoenix households have already received assistance through the first-come, first-serve program. About $1.28 million of funding remains available, according to a city spokesperson.
 Households may only receive assistance through the program one time. To qualify, participants must be Phoenix residents who had a complete loss of SNAP on or after Oct. 1, 2025, or must have had a complete loss of CHIP on or after Oct. 1, 2026, and have not had benefits restored.
 Participants can apply online at phoenix.gov/BenefitLossAssistance .
 Phoenix’s Human Services Department is also trying to help households restore benefits they have lost. The Department recently began offering one-on-one appointments to help families complete SNAP applications and understand work requirements for the program.
